name: hadavin-trigger-error (outline; earlier version run in n8n 2.47.7; this version not re-imported)

nodes.name: Error Trigger
nodes.notes: SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written. This workflow ran once for every failed execution of the main workflow, but ONLY while it was published. Imported and not published, n8n logged that it 'is not active and cannot be executed' and nobody was told. So publishing this workflow is a required set-up step. One error workflow can serve many workflows; it is chosen in the main workflow's Workflow Settings.

nodes.name: Build message
nodes.notes: SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written, with typeVersion 3.4: the message held the workflow name, the execution link, the last node and the error text. Keep typeVersion 3.4: with typeVersion 3 n8n ignored 'assignments' and the message was null. The four field paths used here were all in what the Error Trigger delivered. Do not add the request body or any header to the message, and do not pass on the whole error object: its field execution.error.node holds the failing node with all its parameters and notes.

nodes.name: Notify placeholder
nodes.notes: SEEN IN n8n 2.47.7: this node as written (it does nothing). Replace it with the client's chat or e-mail node and send {{ $json.message }}. What lands here by design, because a person must look: a missing business id or document text; a 401, 409, 400 or 413 from the trigger endpoint; and a 503 (busy) in every round of the main workflow's wait-and-sign-again loop, which means the event was NOT accepted.
